deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics and no work by Riemann. It is a printed page (p. 386) of the Göttingen 'Nachrichten von der K. Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften', from the 1864 volume, filed in the 'R.Primzahlen' bundle. Faint mirror-image bleed-through of p. 385 is visible.

(a) Lines 1–6 end the Society's annual report, which runs over from p. 385. The second volume of Gauss's Werke, containing much of his manuscript Nachlass, is nearly finished. It would already have appeared but for unforeseen editorial difficulties.

(b) The rest of the page begins 'Nr. 5. Ueber zwei neue Derivate der salicyligen Säure' by F. Beilstein. The Secretary presented it on 6 December. This is organic chemistry, not mathematics:
- Aldehyde-ammonia treated with HCN and HCl gives alanine plus ammonium chloride (Strecker synthesis). Valeraldehyde-ammonia likewise gives leucine.
- The analogous experiment had not been tried in the aromatic series. Beilstein's explanation is that hydrobenzamide, hydrosalicylamide, etc. were thought to differ in kind from ordinary aldehyde-ammonia.
- Yet these compounds split, when warmed with acids, into ammonia plus the aldehyde (bitter-almond oil, salicylous acid = salicylaldehyde). So they differ from the aliphatic case only in the aldehyde:ammonia ratio: 3 aldehydes to 2 NH3, with loss of 3 H2O.
- Hence an analogous reaction with HCN/HCl was expected.
- The next page reports the result: C21H18N2O3 + HCN + HCl -> C22H16N2O3 + NH4Cl, product named yellow 'Hydrocyansalid'.

There is no derivation, formula, or computation by Riemann to reconstruct. The page's presence in the bundle is presumably incidental: either reuse of a printed sheet as scrap paper, or archival filing. Nothing in Riemann's hand is visible on this side.
errors: No mathematical errors, since there is no mathematical content.
Chemistry check (my own): the hydrosalicylamide formula C21H18N2O3 equals 3 C7H6O2 + 2 NH3 - 3 H2O, which is consistent.
Chemistry check (my own): the next page's equation C21H18N2O3 + HCN + HCl = C22H16N2O3 + NH4Cl is atom-balanced.

results.modern_name: Strecker synthesis / aminonitrile formation applied to aromatic imines (hydrobenzamides)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a printed journal page (Göttingen Nachrichten 1864) containing a society report and a chemistry article by Beilstein. It contains no mathematical content and nothing written by Riemann.

checkable.asserts: The equation C21H18N2O3 + CHN + HCl = C22H16N2O3 + NH4Cl (from p. 387) balances in C, H, N and O (Cl trivially).
Three salicylaldehyde (C7H6O2) plus two NH3 minus three H2O gives C21H18N2O3, the hydrosalicylamide formula.
